items.title: Tries up, penalties down
items.line: Top-ten Tests in 2026 average 8.1 tries and just 1.5 penalty goals.

items.title: How often does the favourite win?
items.line: 76% of the time since 2000. When it is too close to call, only 59%.

items.title: Japan v Fiji: the trend
items.line: Fiji won 11 of the first 12 meetings since 2003. Japan have won 2 of the last 5.

items.title: Is home advantage real?
items.line: New Zealand win 73% of their away Tests since 2000. England and France win about 70% at home.

items.title: Rugby's scoring explosion
items.line: Top-ten Tests averaged 19 points in the 1960s. In the 2020s it's 50.

items.title: Who beats who?
items.line: Scotland have played New Zealand 33 times and never won. Wales v France is dead level.

items.title: Who has the biggest pack?
items.line: Twenty years of starting eights by weight, with the top three trading places.

items.title: Six Nations title race
items.line: 143 years in 60 seconds. England and Wales are level on 39 titles each.

items.title: Most Test wins of all time
items.line: England led for decades. New Zealand moved ahead for good in 2012.

items.title: Who rules world rugby?
items.line: Thirty years of the top ten, rebuilt from every Test result since 1990.
